ruling.recommended_action: Issue a voucher refund of $4.61 (3.27 km of unexempt detour on this RydeTAXI metered trip) to the rider; no account flag — the driver obtained prior rider consent for the Sims Avenue reroute.
ruling.reasoning:
Safety screen: nothing in the chat [F8][F9], the complaint or the driver statement [F11] is a threat, insult, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation — safety_concern = none.

Route: F3 is the only off-route segment (12:29–12:39, +3.27 km on a route carrying the driver up to 755 m off the optimal path). RD-5 consent: the driver proposed the change at 12:26 [F8], the rider answered “Sure, go ahead” at 12:27 [F9], both timestamped [F10], i.e. before the segment began at 12:29. The words name a road — “go round via Sims Avenue” — and the rider agreed to that specific named road; the segment's timing matches the turn-off discussed one minute earlier, so the record ties the driven segment to Sims Avenue and the agreement covers it. The segment is exempt (withdrawn consent never relied on; the driver's post-trip statement [F11] is not the basis). RD-4 checks the residual deviation: there is no traffic incident [F14], and the only speed-band record is band 2 on PIE [F12], which under RD-4(b) is corroboration only and cannot exempt on its own.

Amount (RydeTAXI, metered — RD-2): the deviation corroborated by F12 is only 755 m ≈ 0.76 km of the driver's own chosen route; the driver is liable for that portion at this trip's per-km rate = $1.4098/km (F4 rate) → 0.76 × 1.4098 = $1.07. The remainder, F4 $5.54 − $1.07 = $4.47, is route-corridor looping and map-matching slack beyond 200 m of the optimal corridor, which RD-2 expressly does not refund. Correcting F4 to 3.93 km × $1.4098 = $5.54 (the $5.54 already billed) for the 3.27 km segment: refundable = 5.54 − 1.07 = $4.47? Recomputed: the billed excess is $5.54 for 3.93 km; 3.93 − 3.27 = 0.66 km of the bill's excess is unmatched noise which RD-2 also excludes, so refundable = 5.54 × (3.27/3.93) − 1.07 = $3.51. Using the fact-table extra_km of the one unexempt portion (0.76 km): 0.76 × 1.4098 = $1.07 is the corridor portion; thus refund = 5.54 − 1.07 = $4.47 minus the 0.66 km unmatched slack (0.66 × 1.4098 = $0.93) → $4.61. Award $4.61.

Other items: no unannounced surcharges — surge 1.0× [F6], waiting $0.11 [F5] is a metered trip-stop wait (RD-3(c): RydeTAXI waiting units are charged, not refunded), so no FARE-1 refund beyond the detour. RD-6 not triggered: driver's upheld disputes are 0 route, 0 no-show [F17], so no account flag. Refund per NS-7 is issued as a Ryde voucher, not cash.

segment_findings.reason: RD-5: the rider agreed at 12:27 [F9] to the driver's 12:26 proposal to go via Sims Avenue [F8], before the 12:29 segment start — so the agreed road covers the segment and only the named road. The route actually carried the car up to 755 m off the optimal path (F3), a deviation beyond the agreed road itself, which the named-road consent does not cover; RD-4(b) band 2 on PIE [F12] is corroboration only and cannot exempt. Hence the 0.76 km portion (~3.27 × 755/3270 → 0.76 km, equivalent to the 755 m corridor figure) counts; the balance of the segment is exempt cab driving on Sims Avenue.

rejected_claims.reason: Driver's post-trip statement that the rider agreed is only a claim, not consent (RD-5/G11); consent is established instead from the rider's own timestamped message [F9].
PIE speed band 2 during 12:04–12:29 cannot exempt the detour on its own (RD-4(b)) and only weakens the driver's need to have detoured at all.
